review_notes: I read the whole target file (154 lines) and inspected the relevant definitions and lemmas in Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex/Circle.lean (AddCircle.toCircle, injective_toCircle), Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Circle.lean (Circle.exp, coeHom, toUnits), Mathlib/Topology/Instances/AddCircle/Real.lean (ZMod.toAddCircle, toAddCircle_injective), Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Basic.lean (mem_rootsOfUnity, rootsOfUnityUnitsMulEquiv, restrictRootsOfUnity), Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/EnoughRootsOfUnity.lean (HasEnoughRootsOfUnity, MulEquiv.hasEnoughRootsOfUnity, natCard_rootsOfUnity), Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Complex.lean (Complex.mem_rootsOfUnity, norm_eq_one_of_mem_rootsOfUnity), Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean (IsPrimitive, zmod_char_primitive_of_eq_one_only_at_zero), and Mathlib/Algebra/Group/AddChar.lean (AddChar structure, map_zero_eq_one, map_add_eq_mul). The `ZMod.val`-based formulas in this file mostly have integer-lifted counterparts (toCircle_intCast, stdAddChar_coe) already; the one statement that does not is the roots-of-unity composite evaluation at lines 139-143, which is the finding below. I did not find a stronger, clearly beneficial generalisation of the AddCircle.toCircle_addChar definition, the injectivity lemmas, or the HasEnoughRootsOfUnity instance that is supported by the sources I read. Uncertainty: I did not compile the proposed proposition and cannot guarantee it elaborates as written; its proof should follow from rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv_apply (line 135-137) and ZMod.toCircle_intCast (lines 53-54).

findings.excerpt:
open Real in
lemma rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv_comp_rootsOfUnityAddChar_val (j : ZMod n) :
    (rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv n (ZMod.rootsOfUnityAddChar n j)).val
      = Complex.exp (2 * π * I * j.val / n) := by
findings.problem: The statement fixes the particular canonical representative `ZMod.val` of the class `j`. This is the only remaining occurrence of `ZMod.val` in the file's root-of-unity part, although the file itself flags `ZMod.val` formulas as "evil" and recommends lifting to `ℤ` (see the docstring on `toCircle_apply`, lines 64-67) and already provides the representative-free `toCircle_intCast` (lines 53-54). As written, the lemma cannot be applied directly to an arbitrary integer lift `k` with `(k : ZMod n) = j`, so users who have an integer exponent must first convert it to `val`.
findings.proposed_change:
State the result for an integer input, mirroring `toCircle_intCast`, e.g.

lemma rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv_comp_rootsOfUnityAddChar_intCast (j : ℤ) :
    (rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv n (ZMod.rootsOfUnityAddChar n (j : ZMod n))).val
      = Complex.exp (2 * π * I * j / n)

and, if the `ZMod.val` form is still wanted, derive the existing lemma from it (or keep it as a corollary). The proof should be `simp [rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv_apply, ZMod.toCircle_intCast]`, since `rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv_apply` (lines 135-137) reduces the composite to the underlying `Circle` value and `toCircle_intCast` evaluates it. The degenerate case `n ≥ 1` is covered by the section's `[NeZero n]`; `j = 0` reduces to `exp 0 = 1`.
findings.benefit: Users with integer representatives (the recommended style in this file and used elsewhere, e.g. `ZMod.toCircle_intCast` in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/ZMod.lean`) get the value formula directly, without choosing the canonical `ZMod.val` representative; this also keeps the roots-of-unity API consistent with the integer-cast API for `toCircle` and `stdAddChar`.

evidence.excerpt:
Explicit formula for `toCircle j`. Note that this is "evil" because it uses `ZMod.val`. Where
possible, it is recommended to lift `j` to `ℤ` and use `toCircle_intCast` instead.

lemma toCircle_intCast (j : ℤ) :
    toCircle (j : ZMod N) = exp (2 * π * I * j / N) := by

@[simp] lemma rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv_apply (w : rootsOfUnity n Circle) :
    ((rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv n w).val : ℂ) = ((w.val : Circle) : ℂ) :=
